cost.description: All costs for providing FAIR data in OSTrails, as detailed in the FAIR section of this document, have been included in the project's overall budget in accordance with Horizon Europe grant eligibility criteria. The Financial Coordination has accounted for the necessary human capacity of data managers, as well as the infrastructure and services required for their effective operation, in its financial distribution.

format:
Most of the activities that will be performed in OSTrails leading to the project deliverables and results stem from co-designing, validating and assessing services, supporting material and the pathways for planning, tracking and assessing research in different contexts and domains. The dataset types and formats are an extension of those activities characterising their nature, scientific relevance and agreed implementation across providers.
  • The types of collected data from landscaping and co-creation activities (such as hackathons, requirements solicitation from pilots, etc) are expected to be in tabular and text formats, e.g. comma separated values and word documents. Additionally, video and photographs of participants in cocreation activities will be collected in .mp4 and .jpg formats. For the architecture and the pathways, excalidraw formatted files will be curated and converted to more open solutions, such as OpenDocument format.
  • The reused data from catalogues, repositories and CRIS systems are provided in different formats according to content and preservation policies of their managed institutions and thematic infrastructures and to used services for collecting the data. Examples are: .json, .txt, .tab, .csv. It should be noted that some sources can be collectively downloaded in .xml and .zip formatted files.
  • The reused data from SKGs are provided in different formats, including semantics exchange to be exploited also programmatically, such as .json, .tar and SQL databases..
  • Output data resulting from software processes are subject to agreements between providers that will be available and documented in the “Commons”, for example .json for DMPs, .xml for SKGs, .txt and .csv for FAIR assessment results.

data_quality_assurance:
CITE is the quality assurance manager of the project tasked with developing and applying quality procedures to monitor and ensure a seamless and high-quality delivery of OSTrails and its results. In addition, the Quality Assurance Board identifies any risks and performs internal project peer review of results. The Project Handbook details some primary processes and policies in this regard. Overall, these depend on the activity that will produce data, according to which there may be:
  1. Data conforming to format specifications.
  2. Use of tools for automatic checks to validate content.
  3. Code review of data analysis code.
  4. Consistency verified with data models and standards.
At the meta-level, the project will design and deliver a general-purpose SKG Research Product Quality toolbox that will allow authoritative individuals (e.g., PIs, authors, curators, librarians) to annotate SKG contents using SKG common APIs derived from WP1. Quality indicators include, but are not limited to, coverage, accuracy, timeliness, coherence. OSTrails focuses also on the quality of FAIR assessment processes and will create a benchmark environment for quality control over all legacy and future tests, to ensure that all assessment tools behave correctly and consistently.

distribution.available_until:
The open access policies and data agreements with scientific publishers will be carefully reviewed before deciding to publish in these venues so that they are fully Open Access. As a minimum, the consortium will publish in Green OA (self-archiving) deposited in Zenodo or thematic repository of the research infrastructures at the time of submission (preprints) and update with Author Manuscript (post-print). The consortium will also prioritise platforms that practice open peer review, when possible, such as the Open Research Europe (ORE). This ensures there are no delays in the immediate access to publications, and their underlying data, and enhances transparency in the process. Special attention is given to the immediate and/or early sharing of data underlying our publications.
At this moment, it is not determined whether any partner would like to seek protection of their IPR. If and when that arises during the OSTrails lifetime, the DMP will be updated accordingly.

The OSTrails deposited data will remain available and findable for at least 20 years according to the policy of Zenodo. More information will follow in the sustainability plan of the project, but at this stage, no retraction of access is expected from the consortium partners outside of this timeframe.

security_and_privacy.description: Data stored in One Drive institutional storage are backed up incrementally or regularly as part of data security measures followed by the respective institutional providers, mainly Microsoft. For an extra layer of security, OSTrails partners will follow the 3-2-1 back up rule where 3 copies of the data (production data and 2 backup copies) are stored on two different media (disk and tape) with one copy off-site for disaster recovery. The same applies for Zenodo that generates backups of live content and keeps it in disk storage capabilities. For secure access to the data, servers will be protected by passwords and firewalls. Data that appear to have privacy constraints and applicable ethical norms will be anonymised and made public only in aggregated form (no raw data will be shared).

dataset.description:
The OpenAIRE Graph is exported as several dataseta, so you can download the parts you are interested into.

publication_[part].tar: metadata records about research literature (includes types of publications listed here)
dataset_[part].tar: metadata records about research data (includes the subtypes listed here) 
software.tar: metadata records about research software (includes the subtypes listed here)
otherresearchproduct_[part].tar: metadata records about research products that cannot be classified as research literature, data or software (includes types of products listed here)
organization.tar: metadata records about organizations involved in the research life-cycle, such as universities, research organizations, funders.
datasource.tar: metadata records about data sources whose content is available in the OpenAIRE Graph. They include institutional and thematic repositories, journals, aggregators, funders' databases.
project.tar: metadata records about project grants.
relation_[part].tar: metadata records about relations between entities in the graph.
communities_infrastructures.tar: metadata records about research communities and research infrastructures

Each file is a tar archive containing gz files, each with one json per line. Each json is compliant to the schema available at http://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10519039. The documentation for the model is available at https://graph.openaire.eu/docs/data-model/

Learn more about the OpenAIRE Graph at https://graph.openaire.eu.

Discover the graph's content on OpenAIRE EXPLORE and our API for developers.

dmp.description:
This deliverable reflects the data and software management activities of the OSTrails Horizon Europe project. OSTrails will enhance the planning, tracking, and assessing of scientific knowledge production by delivering the commons to streamline FAIRness, interconnectivity and foster harmonised adoption of data practices within the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) ecosystem. The project onboards Scientific Knowledge Graphs (SKGs), Data Management Planning platforms, and FAIR assessment tools, and engages with thematic and national Open Science and EOSC communities to co-develop and test tailored pathways supporting seamless information exchange and automated processes. These are:
  • FAIR assessment tools: FAIR Evaluator, Metadata Validator, FAIR-Aware, FOOPS!, FAIROS
  • DMP platforms: ARGOS, DaMAP, Data Stewardship Wizard, Sikt DMP
  • SKGs: OpenAIRE Graph, CLARIN VLO, CESSDA Data Catalogue, SSH Open Marketplace, Software Heritage, LifeBlock SKG and LifeWatch Catalogue, JERICO KG, SOCIB KG, PUMA, 8 National CRIS platforms
As it becomes evident, OSTrails operates at the meta-level, given that Data Management Plans (DMPs) and FAIRness are core component of OSTrails, the results enabling machine actionable DMPs and their evaluation according to set rubrics, will be applied and followed by future iterations of the DMP. Thus, our DMP will equally serve as a pilot to test our project outputs at a larger scale (in accordance with WP4, T4.4 Horizon Europe pilot). The OSTrails DMP will be treated as a “living document” that will be continuously updated to record progress and changes in the decisions of data, software and other research outputs management practices followed by the consortium. All iterations, particularly M18 and M36, will be available and linked in the published DMP record on Zenodo: OSTrails (zenodo.org).
The structure of D6.1 “Data Management Plan” follows the European Commission’s Horizon Europe Data Management Plan Template topics and answers the contained questions with information that members have in this initial phase of the project. It should be noted that answers relevant to Section “Other Research Outputs” from the EC’s template reflect software development. At the end, we provide specific examples of data, software and other research outputs that the project will be generating, collecting or reusing.
